newsitem.title: PERU: Powerfin to buy Southern Peru plant.
newsitem.headline: Powerfin to buy Southern Peru plant.

text.p: Copper miner Southern Peru Ltd said Tuesday it has reached an agreement to sell a power plant to Belgium's Powerfin SA for $44 million.
The companies also agreed Powerfin would supply Peru's largest copper miner with electricity for 20 years, Southern said in a statement.
Southern said Powerfin agreed to make sufficient investments to increase energy supply from the plant to satisfy the miner's expansion plans.

"Currently, Southern generates 130 kilowatts per hour (KWh) and will need more when it concludes the expansion of its Cuajone mine and the modernization of the Ilo smelter," the company statement added.

The copper miner plans to invest $1 billion expanding its Cuajone mine and modernising the Ilo smelter in Peru. The first approved investment stage will spend $245 million to raise total copper production at Cuajone by 26 percent.
Construction will start in 1997 and expanded output will start coming on stream in 1999.
In the second, $787 million stage, the engineering for the modernisation of the Ilo smelter has been approved. Start-up would be in 2001 to eventually capture 95 percent of the sulphur emissions.

Majority owned by ASARCO Inc and Peru's largest copper producer, Southern accounts for about 60 percent of Peru's total copper output from its Cuajone and Toquepala open-pit mines, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
